newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish T-bills to stay flat as rates seen steady.
newsitem.headline: Polish T-bills to stay flat as rates seen steady.

text.p: Polish T-bill yields are expected to hold steady at next Monday's primary tender as expectations of an interest rate change in the near-term faded despite upbeat September inflation estimates, analysts said on Friday.

Most T-bill yields were expected to stay flat on Monday after the central bank said this week real interst rates would rise in coming months. Analysts saw those comments as a sign nominal rates would remain steady for now.

Even if year-on-year inflation falls to 19 percent in September from 20.5 in August, the central bank was not likely to cut nominal rates, analysts said. They said the central bank would not want to stimulate credit action, which boomed after the last rate cut in July.
Finance Minister Grzegorz Kolodko on Friday forecast year-on-year price growth in September was 18.9 percent.
In addition, the treasury's relatively large one billion zloty T-bill offer on Monday would likely absorb more bids and keep yields buoyed, analysts said.
"Yields of longer paper are likely to stay flat on Monday. There even might be a small tendency to rise," said Marta Tabor, T-bill dealer at Pekao SA.
Analysts said domestic investors would likely bid for about 1.2 billion zlotys worth of bills, but it was not clear whether foreign investors would be active on Monday.

"It is a relatively large offer, but demand should top it. However, it is still not clear whether foreign investors will show up on Monday after this week's statements by the National Bank of Poland," said Wojciech Kowalczyk of Bank Handlowy SA.
Analysts expected the average yield on the benchmark 52-week bill to be around 19.45 percent, just up from 19.43 percent at this week's primary auction.
They said the average yields of the 26- and 13-week paper should be relatively flat from last week's 18.55 and 19.09 percent, respectively.
The yield on the shortest 8-week paper was seen down from 18.18 percent on September 26, the last auction at which the bill was offered, helped corporate clients' strong demand.
On Monday, the treasury will offer 550 million zlotys of the bechmark, 100 million zlotys of 26-week bills, 200 million 13-week bills and 150 million of the 8-week paper.
Analysts were mixed on whether one-day money market rates would ease next week to the the level of the NBP's main 14-day reverse repo rate, last at 19.14 percent.

Downward pressure on one-day rates could come if the NBP continues to keep its main drainage rate flat. But small cash inflows from reverse repo buy backs and NBP-bill redemptions next week could counter that and keep demand for cash high.

Analysts said next Tuesday's 700 million zloty auction of 10-year floating bonds, maturing October 18, 2006, was not likely to generate much interest, which should keep rates basically flat from the last auction on September 10.
Last month, the average price of the 10-year paper, whose coupon is one basis point above the average 52-week T-bill yield for two months before a particular interest term, was 99.73.

Analysts expected the zloty to remain between 1.6 and 1.9 percent below the centre of its 14-percent trading band, established with the help from foreign zloty purchases when the zloty was weak and sales when the unit firmed.

"It seems that foreigners are eager to buy the zloty when it falls to around 1.6 percent from parity, which pushes the currency back towards resistance at 1.9 percent," said Mateusz Bieniek of Societe Generale in Warsaw.
The zloty closed the week at 2.8150/60 per dollar and at 1.8385/95 per mark, or about 1.80 percent from the parity rate.
